entities.summary: Tedald, also known as Theodald, Theodaldus, Tedaldus, Tedaldo, Teodaldus, Teodaltus, or Teodaldo, was the forty-third Bishop of Arezzo from 1023 until his death on June 18, 1036. Born in Italy, Tedald was a prominent figure in the medieval Christian church, and his tenure as Bishop of Arezzo was marked by significant ecclesiastical reforms. Under his leadership, the Bishopric of Arezzo played a crucial role in the development of the Catholic Church in the region, and Tedald's legacy continued to influence the church's governance and doctrine for centuries to come. One of the most striking aspects of Tedald's legacy is the enduring impact of his reforms on the development of the Catholic Church in Italy. As a testament to his enduring influence, the Cathedral of Arezzo, which he oversaw during his tenure as Bishop, remains one of the most iconic landmarks in the city to this day. In the centuries following his death, Tedald's name became synonymous with the ideals of Christian unity and reform, and his legacy continues to inspire scholars and theologians to this day. Theodald's remarkable career serves as a powerful reminder of the enduring importance of religious leadership and the critical role that individuals like Tedald have played in shaping the course of human history.
